proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level result is Kennedy et al.'s nonprivate pointwise-CATE frontier; the strict delta is a pure-private two-branch frontier on its exact-uniform two-scale subclass together with an attaining finite mechanism. The closest privacy result for CATE is Schröder et al.'s Gaussian approximate-private release, which neither treats pure privacy nor derives a minimax rate. The closest method result is Chaudhuri et al.'s private U-statistic stabilization, which addresses a fixed kernel rather than composite target fibers with unknown causal nuisances. The occupancy identity makes the dense transition auditable, while the proposal keeps the remaining full-fiber entropy cancellation visible as its central open question.

seed_details.anchor: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 and the downgraded parent proposal's full-fiber lifting question
seed_details.anchor_read: Kennedy et al., Introduction, Theorems 1--2, Section 5 construction, and Discussion; the parent core, pair-score nodes, and bank README.
seed_details.kernel: Derive and attain \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) over the full exact-uniform unknown-propensity Hölder class by occupancy-weighted full-fiber projections.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the parent's indicator of exactly two records by \(N_jB_j\), prove constant replacement sensitivity, and then establish a nuisance-independent weighted-shell bound.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for pure-private pointwise CATE minimax rates and occupancy-normalized private causal U-statistics located approximate-private CATE releases and generic private U-statistics, but no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.novelty_check: The adjacent papers separately provide occupancy weighting, private projection stabilization, private test aggregation, and coupling converses; none proves a pure-private full-class pointwise-CATE frontier or the required entropy-free score certificate.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Chaudhuri et al. because local Hájek projection already privatizes every bounded U-statistic.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem treats one fixed kernel; the load-bearing problem is a uniformly oriented composite score over unknown CATE nuisances with a shell bound independent of the growing profile class.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, main degenerate-kernel theorem, local Hájek reweighting algorithm, sensitivity proof, and Discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the Gaussian, Gaussian--Laplace convolution, and privacy-dominated limit laws of the occupancy-weighted pointwise-CATE projection as \(n\ell^d\) crosses one.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition the Hoeffding decomposition on multinomial occupancies before studentizing the privacy noise, rather than applying a fixed-kernel variance bound.
seed_details.target_method_search: No located paper derives a pure-private pointwise-CATE limit law with occupancy-varying degeneracy; Kennedy et al. explicitly leave distribution theory open.
seed_details.novelty_check: The CATE paper leaves limit theory open, the occupancy paper is global and nonprivate, and the private CATE paper uses approximate-private Gaussian perturbations; the exact transition law is unoccupied.
seed_details.red_team: A routine triangular-array central limit theorem plus independent Laplace noise settles the claim.
seed_details.rebuttal: The first projection changes order at the occupancy elbow and the privacy calibration is data-dependent, so neither the normalization nor the limiting convolution is fixed across regimes.

seed_details.anchor: The downgraded parent proposal's weighted-shell risk proposition
seed_details.anchor_read: The parent weighted-shell proposition, one-record obstruction, sparse pair theorem, rejected angle diagnostic, and reviewer strengthening path.
seed_details.kernel: On an explicit wavelet sieve of dimension \(K\), construct one-sensitive profiled pair scores with a shell functional bounded uniformly in \(K\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Profile composite pair contrasts before exponential selection and replace the finite-cover union bound by direct scalar-shell integration.
seed_details.target_method_search: Asi et al. and Birgé-type T-estimation retain cover complexity; no located pure-private CATE theorem cancels a growing nuisance sieve.
seed_details.novelty_check: The finite-dimensional result would be new only if its shell constant is uniform in sieve dimension; without that uniformity the generic cover results subsume it.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely a finite-dimensional version of the parent's open question.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniformity in \(K\) is the exact compactness certificate needed for the infinite-dimensional lift, but the result is retained as a pilot rather than the headline.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1 and 3, quasi-oracle theorem, influence-function calibration proof, and Discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize a local asymptotic minimax efficiency envelope for pointwise CATE when \(\epsilon=\epsilon_n\) shrinks and determine when pure privacy changes the efficient limit experiment.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gaussian smooth-sensitivity output perturbation by a pure-private local experiment and derive its convolution bound before seeking an attaining estimator.
seed_details.target_method_search: The closest CATE release is approximate-private and gives quasi-oracle risk, while the pointwise Hölder target is irregular and lacks a classical semiparametric information bound.
seed_details.red_team: Pointwise Hölder CATE is nonregular, so a semiparametric efficiency bound is the wrong object.
seed_details.rebuttal: A local asymptotic minimax envelope may exist after rate normalization, but the missing differentiable experiment makes this less feasible than the selected minimax lane.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction's policy consumer, Theorems 1--2, higher-order estimator construction, and Discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Derive pure-private regret for plug-in treatment rules under a margin condition when the CATE rate has both nuisance and occupancy privacy elbows.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert pointwise or uniform CATE error into welfare regret under a margin law, then privatize policy selection without repeatedly spending privacy across candidate rules.
seed_details.target_method_search: Private policy-learning papers exist, but the gaps substrate contains no theorem-level policy-class comparator and no margin-class evidence sufficient to pin a sharp new regret frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The regret bound is a standard plug-in corollary of any private CATE rate.
seed_details.rebuttal: A matching private policy lower bound could avoid that objection, but the necessary policy-class substrate is absent here.

seed_details.anchor_read: Discussion's explicit inference question together with the model and higher-order construction.
seed_details.kernel: Invert privatized local randomization or conformity scores to obtain finite-sample pointwise-CATE confidence sets.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify a valid symmetry orbit for observational records before calibrating a private conformity score.
seed_details.target_method_search: The observational Hölder model supplies neither exchangeable residuals nor a known assignment group; no exact symmetry survives unknown propensity without adding a new design assumption.
seed_details.red_team: Conformal validity is unavailable because the causal counterfactual score is not exchangeable under observational treatment.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds on the present substrate, so the seed is rejected rather than repaired by an unrelated randomization assumption.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction and main fixed- and random-design theorems, random-design construction, lower-bound proof boundary, and further discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Prove equivalence between uniform-cell and public-mass-weighted private frontiers for every known design density bounded above and below, or derive the density-geometry divergence threshold.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace equal-volume identities by public cell masses in the pair normalization and bound the resulting maximum record influence before transporting Hölder smoothness.
seed_details.target_method_search: Gao and Han expose nonprivate design geometry, and private regression handles pointwise localization, but no located paper transfers an unknown-propensity pure-private CATE pair mechanism across design densities.
seed_details.red_team: A public probability-integral transform immediately reduces known density to uniform design.
seed_details.rebuttal: In dimensions above one, transport can distort Hölder constants and cell aspect ratios, so equivalence requires a regular transport theorem or fails through a geometry term.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--2, one-shot multiscale estimator, pointwise adaptive lower bound, and Discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Find the exact logarithmic price for adapting simultaneously to CATE smoothness, nuisance smoothness, and occupancy under pure central privacy.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace density coefficients in the correlated one-shot release by orthogonal causal projection coefficients and track the privacy covariance across nuisance and localization scales.
seed_details.target_method_search: The located adaptive-private results concern density estimation under federated or local privacy; no result combines the CATE nuisance elbow with central pure privacy and cell occupancy.
seed_details.red_team: This simply applies private Lepski selection to the oracle estimators at each smoothness level.
seed_details.rebuttal: Repeated private releases are rate-suboptimal in the cited adaptation theorem, and the causal score family adds an unknown nuisance-product scale, but the fixed-class estimator must be solved first.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel is anchored to Kennedy et al.'s Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, which fix the pointwise Hölder-CATE class, the nonprivate elbow, and the localized higher-order proof architecture. Zeng et al.'s Section 4 supplies the occupancy-conditioned treated--control construction showing that cells with more than two records should be weighted rather than discarded. Chaudhuri et al.'s local Hájek-projection algorithm and sensitivity proof supply the record-influence stabilization move for second-order scores. Asi et al.'s Section 4 T-mechanism supplies clipped stable testing and exponential selection, while the proposed ordered-shell functional replaces its global cover count. Acharya et al.'s private Le Cam and Assouad coupling arguments supply the same-class converse. Searches of pure-private pointwise CATE, occupancy-normalized causal U-statistics, and full-function private CATE found only Niu et al. and Schröder et al.; these provide general or approximate-private releases, not the target minimax frontier. Balcer and Vadhan establish a structurally analogous sparse--dense representation divide for histograms, not causal projection scores. No closer paper was found that subsumes the occupancy-weighted full-fiber kernel.
